page: OVHcloud bm-l1 belongs to the Metal server family and runs on the KVM hypervisor utilizing the x86_64 instruction set architecture. Compute resources consist of 16 dedicated vCPUs clocked at 3.1 GHz, avoiding noisy-neighbor overhead commonly seen in shared multi-tenant environments. System memory totals 128.0 GB, which equals 8.0 GB per virtual processor. This 1:8 compute-to-memory configuration establishes the instance within a memory-optimized operational profile.

Storage and network provisions are bundled directly with the hardware profile. Disk storage includes 1920 GB of local NVMe SSD media, offering high local transfer speeds and lower access latencies compared to network-attached storage tiers. Network connectivity operates at a baseline rate of 1 Gbps, and the configuration allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The instance does not include dedicated graphics processing units, centering compute tasks strictly on the x86_64 host processor cores.

From a resource balance perspective, bm-l1 delivers substantial memory capacity and high-speed local NVMe capacity per core, though networking is restricted to a 1 Gbps baseline. The absence of hardware cryptographic and vector execution extensions, as indicated in the hardware capability flags, limits throughput for vector-heavy mathematical routines or specialized cryptographic transforms. However, the dedicated core allocation combined with an 8.0 GB-per-vCPU ratio and nearly 2 TB of NVMe storage makes this configuration practical for in-memory databases, Redis caches, analytical processing systems, local data transformation pipelines, and relational database hosting.
description: OVHcloud bm-l1 is a Metal instance built on x86_64 architecture and managed via KVM virtualization. The system provides 16 dedicated vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 3.1 GHz alongside 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing a memory-dense ratio of 8.0 GB per virtual core. Local storage is bundled directly with a single 1920 GB NVMe solid-state drive, delivering low-latency disk operations without relying exclusively on remote volumes. Network connectivity provides a baseline throughput of 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default. Without hardware GPU accelerators present, the server emphasizes compute memory balance and local NVMe capacity. Qualitative resource efficiency stems from the combination of high memory density and dedicated high-speed local disk capacity within a 16-core footprint. This resource allocation aligns with memory-heavy workloads, operational databases, caching tiers, analytics engines, and high-throughput backend services requiring stable CPU execution.
